title.narrative: Women and Youth Leadership and Participation

description.narrative: Contract related to: Women and Youth Leadership and Participation - The proposed Action intents to contribute to Specific-Objective 1.3: Support CSOs as actors of good governance and development in partner countries and to the achievement of the related result 1.3: Civil Society Organisations¿ (CSOs) ability to engage as actors of good governance and development at country level is improved.The Action rolls out the EU support to country-level CSO initiatives aimed at implementing priorities reflected in the NDICI-GLOBAL Europe, Annex III CSO Thematic Programme and the subsequent draft Multiannual Indicative Plan for the same. In line with the policy of geographisation, a majority of funds under the CSO MAAP 2021-2024, will be allocated under the Action to support civil society in partner countries in Africa, Asia and the Pacific, Latin America and Caribbean, and in Neighbourhood countries and Russia. Activities funded under the Action will support a broad range of civil society actors including and prioritising, but not limited to, women and youth organisations, In the framework of the Country Roadmaps for EU and Member States engagement with civil society (CSO Roadmaps), all initiatives under the Action will aim at and contribute to strengthening civil society partner¿s institutional and operational capacity through a comprehensive approach; enabling and ensuring their participation; and on improving the environment in which they operate. Particular attention will be paid to CSOs capacities to benefit from the digital transformation which will pay attention to accessible digital technology and reduce the gap on access to ICT.

title.narrative: Proportion of seats held by women in (a) national parliaments and (b) local governments

description.narrative: SDG indicator 5.5.1 under (a) measures the proportion of seats held by women in (a) national parliaments, currently as at 1 January of reporting year, is currently measured as the number of seats held by women members in single or lower chambers of national parliaments, expressed as a percentage of all occupied seats. National parliaments can be bicameral or unicameral. This indicator covers the single chamber in unicameral parliaments and the lower chamber in bicameral parliaments. It does not cover the upper chamber of bicameral parliaments. Seats are usually won by members in general parliamentary elections. Seats may also be filled by nomination, appointment, indirect election, rotation of members and byelection. Seats refer to the number of parliamentary mandates, or the number of members of parliament.Data reported against SDG indicators can be retrieved from the official UN SDG Database and Statistics https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/unsdg. title.narrative: Outcome 2Strengthened movements, institutions, and CSOs advocating for increased participation and leadership of women and youth

description.narrative: Strong movements, institutions, and CSOs are essential for effective lobbying and advocacy work that ensures women and youth fully engage and take leadership positions in Zimbabwean governance and decisionmaking processes at all levels. This result area aims to address the issue of weak movements and institutions, which are now exacerbated by fragmentation and a lack of coordination among CSOs working on womens and youth empowerment. To close these gaps, the action would provide training and capacity building for CSOs in order to encourage women and youths to participate in leadership and governance processes. They will be supported through a mentorship trajectory aimed at strengthening their interpersonal, communication, critical thinking, and public speaking abilities, which are essential in leadership, governance and holding duty bearers accountable. Furthermore, movements and CSOs will be supported on how to identify contemporary advocacy asks to champion including working with the media and develop advocacy plans. Success of the action will include a better coordinated women and youth movement advocating in a coordinate manner at local and national level.

title.narrative: Outcome 1Increased capacity of women, youth champions, CSO, and newly elected officials in planning, budgeting, accountability, and decision making

description.narrative: This result area addresses the inadequate capacity of women, youth, and their CSOs to participate and assume leadership roles in planning, budgeting, accountability, and decisionmaking platforms (e.g., council meetings on planning and budgeting, parliamentary constituency meetings, and any national consultation forum). Currently, women and youth lack the information, skills, and agency to fully participate in civic responsibilities such as influencing policy during national, provincial, and municipal planning and budgeting procedures. In addition, women and youth lack the ability to hold dutybearers accountable. In addition, the majority of women and youth who are elected for the first time as Members of Parliament have little capacity to effectively execute their constitutional mandate in legislation, oversight, and representation to influence decisionmaking in Parliament. Local implementing partners will support capacity trainings for women and youth, while Hivos will focus on freshly elected politicians.Ultimately, capacity building will empower women, youth, and CSOs to socially transform the status quo, reconstruct their reality, and influence sustainable social change. Individual and collective knowledge and skills gained will widen choices, opportunities and the agency to claim their rights Followup on the actions success will include online participation by the trained women and youth, documentation of their success stories, and learning letters 25 on their experiences in leadership and governance

title.narrative: Outcome 3 Enhanced constitutional implementation on women and youth leadership, participation, and representation

description.narrative: This result area responds to the challenges relating to lack of political goodwill to fully implement provisions of the constitution that deals with women and youth leadership, participation and representation. The action will conduct a number of activities that include direct engagement with dutybearers and increasing pressure through advocacy in order for the constitutional provisions to be adopted and implemented. Women and Youth Leaders will be trained in using the constitutional provisions to advance the considerations for women empowerment and participation in leadership and governance processes at all levels. This will focus on constitutional provisions on equality of women and youth (including the 5050 and the 30% quota at both local and national governments).The Gender Audit, which will be carried out as part of the action, will allow tracking of progress in implementing the recommendations of the baseline audit, which was carried out in 2019. (post 2018 election period). Furthermore, the audit findings will be evidence that will be utilized to hold Government institutions accountable and inform future interventions. The Observatory, on the other hand, will have a multiple role, including watchdog, real time evidence generation and response; supervision, pre, during and post elections, which will generate further evidence that will be used to hold various institutions accountable. In addition, the action will work with MWACSMED on dissemination of the CEDAW national action plan and her other partners to identify key community opinion leaders, male champions and people with a good image in the society and can influence societal decision and bring them together for a conversation around women leadership and respect of their human rights as well involvement in decision making. We will support sensitization activities and dissemination of existing gender equality frameworks and materials to educate the public officials and the society in general on women rights. We aim to contribute to improved gender responsiveness in the government ministries, departments and by the general public. Accountability will be ascertained through regular review of the Hansards, and other platforms available and used by the Women and Youth Leaders when undertaking their advocacy activities and messaging.

description.narrative: To be effective advocates, women and youth, as well as their CSOs, must gain confidence and feel supported by others. To that purpose, we will organise and facilitate learning sessions on (council) local level planning, gender responsive budgeting, and constitutional provisions on gender equality, which will serve as a platform for them and their CSOs. This will enable them to participate in governance processes and future programming, as well as engage, network, and share their knowledge, ideas, and experiences from their leadership journeys. These events will assist women and young people in employing effective techniques and strategies in leadership and governance processes, as well as build their networks and coordination and allow for the documentation of best practises. The Townhall meetings concept will be used as a convening platform for dialoguing between government stakeholders and citizens at various levels of governance. The meetings are consultative in nature and will be convened by the women and youth leaders held within community safe spaces to discuss women and youth participation and leadership. Through this action, women and youth and their organisations will be supported to organize and meaningfully engage with the duty bearers to foster accountability and transparency. Key
